sections.label: Singapore climate change projections
sections.summary: The V3 study projects longer, more frequent dry spells and more extreme daily rainfall in Singapore by 2100.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: Findings from Singapore's Third National Climate Change Study, or V3 study, project that Singapore will see longer and more frequent dry spells by 2100, averaging one every 10 to 60 months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: We also expect more extreme daily rainfall across all seasons which will increase the likelihood of flash floods.

sections.label: Singapore sewerage system extent
sections.summary: Singapore has about 3,600 km of sewers and 48 km of Deep Tunnel Sewerage System.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: Singapore has an extensive sewerage system with about 3,600 kilometres (km) of sewers and 48 km of Deep Tunnel Sewerage System (DTSS).

sections.label: Tanker tracking and locking devices
sections.summary: Clause 42 amends section 74 to empower regulations requiring tankers to be installed with tracking and locking devices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: To deter such illegal actions, clause 42 amends section 74 to empower regulations to be made to impose requirements for these tankers to be installed with tracking and locking devices.

sections.label: Penalty increases for discharge offences
sections.summary: Clauses 12, 13 and 14 raise maximum penalties for repeat offences involving unauthorised trade effluent and hazardous substance discharges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: Clause 12 of the Bill will amend section 16(5) to increase the maximum penalty from $20,000 to $50,000 for repeat offenders who discharge trade effluent without approval or not in accordance with conditions of that approval or regulations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: Clause 13 will amend section 16A(6) relating to the discharge of dangerous or hazardous substances without approval or not in accordance with conditions of that approval or regulations, which causes injury, death, damage to sewers, or severe disruption to treatment, by doubling the maximum penalty for repeat offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: The maximum penalty for repeat offences will thus be raised from $200,000 to $400,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: Clause 14 will amend section 17(4) to increase the maximum penalty from $40,000 to $100,000 for offences relating to the failure to comply with PUB's order to stop and/or treat the discharge of hazardous substances.

sections.label: Minimum penalties for effluent discharge
sections.summary: Clause 17 raises repeat-offence penalties for sewerage damage, and clause 12 sets minimum penalties for illegal trade effluent discharge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: Clause 17 will also amend section 20(2) relating to damage caused to the public sewerage system, increasing the penalty for repeat offences from $200,000 to $400,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: The second enhancement is to introduce minimum penalties for four offences relating to illegal trade effluent discharge, across both first and subsequent offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: Clause 12 will amend section 16(5) to insert a mandatory minimum penalty for discharging trade effluent without approval or not in accordance with conditions of that approval or regulations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: This will be $4,000 for the first offence, and $10,000 for repeat offences.

sections.label: PUB silt control powers extended
sections.summary: Clause 23 amends section 26 to extend PUB's silt control powers to non-construction activities and discharges into reservoirs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: Clause 23 amends section 26 to extend PUB's silt control powers to non-construction activities and discharges into reservoirs.

sections.label: Owners must maintain drainage systems
sections.summary: Clause 20 introduces sections 22A and 22B requiring premises owners to keep stormwater drainage systems, drains and flood protection measures in proper order.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: Clause 20 will introduce new sections 22A and 22B to require owners of premises to keep their stormwater drainage systems, drains and flood protection measures in proper order.

sections.label: PUB rectification of illegal works
sections.summary: Clauses 7, 10, 17 and 21 to 24 let PUB urgently carry out rectification works for illegal alterations, works or damage and recover costs from the culprit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: When there are any illegal alterations, works or damage that affect the public sewerage system, stormwater drainage system, or drain, clauses 7, 10, 17 and 21 to 24 provide for PUB to urgently step in to carry out rectification works to restore the function of the public sewerage system, stormwater drainage system, or drain, and recover the cost of the rectification works from the culprit.

sections.label: Compliance Certificate written notice
sections.summary: Clause 27 amends section 33 to let PUB issue a written notice requiring developments to apply for a Compliance Certificate and penalise non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: To ensure this, clause 27 amends section 33 to enable PUB to issue a written notice requiring developments to apply for a Compliance Certificate which will complete the works certification process and penalise those that fail to comply with the written notice.

sections.label: Drainage systems on private land
sections.summary: Clause 38 inserts section 60A stating certain drainage and sewerage systems on private land do not form part of the land or belong to the landowner.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: Clause 38 inserts a new section 60A to make it clear that certain drainage and sewerage systems built on private land do not form part of the land and do not belong to the landowner.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: We are standardising and clarifying terms used in the SDA, both through clause 2 which clarifies terms, such as "sewerage system" defined in section 2 and through other clauses which remove overlaps in the use of the terms "sewage" and "trade effluent" throughout the Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: Clause 26 inserts a new section 32A to enable the incorporation by reference of PUB's Codes of Practice for both sewerage and drainage to enable PUB to enforce the requirements more effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: In summary, we must protect our sewers from damage and take errant companies to task to better secure our used water system.

sections.label: PUB powers and stakeholder cooperation
sections.summary: The amendments give PUB legislative powers, and premises owners, developers and stakeholders are invited to work with PUB to secure water future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment):
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the SDA I have elaborated on will provide PUB with the legislative powers to do so, and I invite premises owners, developers and stakeholders to work with us and play a part in securing our water future together.

sections.label: Questions on maintenance cost burden
sections.summary: The question asks why the Bill lacks a cost-sharing mechanism and what measures prevent disproportionate maintenance costs for asset-rich, cash-poor households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister explain why this Bill does not incorporate a cost-sharing mechanism for private owners, especially concerning shared drainage facilities between neighbouring properties?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What measures will the Government implement to ensure that "asset-rich and cash-poor" households, such as retired seniors, are not disproportionately burdened by these maintenance costs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Additionally, has the Government conducted a thorough assessment of the cumulative financial impact on residents, particularly those in older estates where ageing infrastructure may require more frequent and costly maintenance?

sections.label: PUB service fee structure
sections.summary: The passage asks how PUB will establish the fee structure for these services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will PUB establish the fee structure for these services?

sections.label: PUB standards and fees concerns
sections.summary: The passage asks whether PUB must publish an impact assessment before significant standards changes and raises concerns on fees, transparency, privacy and consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would PUB be required to publish a comprehensive impact assessment before adopting significant changes to standards?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This would enhance transparency and would allow for informed decision-making.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must ensure that shared responsibilities for maintenance do not become undue financial burdens, especially for vulnerable populations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While emergency powers are necessary for safety, they must be exercised responsibly and transparently, balancing the need for efficiency with residents' rights for privacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: New fees for drainage system maintenance should be transparent and reasonable and the adoption of external standards should prioritise local needs and involve community consultation.

sections.label: PUB prosecutions of companies
sections.summary: Amy Khor told Parliament that since 2014 PUB prosecuted 119 companies for illegal trade effluent discharge, with 21 second-time and 23 repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In Senior Minister of State Amy Khor's reply to an oral Parliamentary Question during the sitting on 6 August 2019, she shared with this House that since 2014, PUB has prosecuted 119 companies for illegal discharge of trade effluent into the sewers, where the discharge did not comply with the stipulations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Khor further shared that of the 119 prosecuted companies, 21 were second-time offenders and another 23 committed the offences more than twice.

sections.label: Minimum fines for offenders
sections.summary: The passage states first-time offenders will face a minimum fine of $40,000 and second or subsequent offenders a minimum fine of $80,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For first-time offenders, there will now be a minimum fine in the sum of $40,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As for the offenders who commit an offence for the second time or more, a minimum fine will also be introduced in the quantum of $80,000.

sections.label: Amendments for hazardous discharge fines
sections.summary: Sections 16, 16A and 17 will be amended to impose minimum fines for offences involving discharge of dangerous or hazardous substances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Sections 16, 16A and 17 will be amended to impose minimum fines for offences relating to discharge of dangerous or hazardous substances.

sections.label: PUB cost recovery powers
sections.summary: The Bill will introduce amendments to refine PUB's powers to recover and apportion costs and expenses as it thinks just.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill will introduce amendments to refine the PUB's powers to recover and apportion costs and expenses as it thinks just.

sections.label: PUB recovered sums quantum
sections.summary: The Senior Minister of State is asked to share the quantum of sums recovered and the types of cases where PUB has taken steps to recover expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State share the quantum of the sums that have been recovered and the types of cases where PUB have taken steps to recover expenses?

sections.label: PUB urgent rectification amendments
sections.summary: The Bill makes eleven amendments to allow PUB to enter any premises without notice to carry out urgent rectification works in emergencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill makes eleven amendments to allow PUB to enter any premises without notice to carry out urgent rectification works in cases of emergency.
